rejected_candidates.reason: These preliminary worst-case and probabilistic product results are explicitly recalled from earlier sources rather than proved in this paper.
They are definitions and modeling assumptions, not finite equality, bound, comparison, or construction conclusions.
They depend on earlier probabilistic inner-product results and are less representative than the paper's transformation-sequence analysis.
It is Tropp's matrix concentration theorem quoted from another source rather than proved in this paper.
The rectangular concentration theorem relies on the delegated Theorem 3.1 and conditional-expectation machinery absent from the frozen bundle.
The paper calls this identity well known and cites Tropp rather than proving it. The former threshold-form target was therefore not a source-faithful task from this paper and was removed.

Their concentration arguments and detailed local-error constructions require a probabilistic proof stack absent from the frozen bundle. P06-T3 retains the exact product-expansion core without promoting the full concentration theorem.
Its loss-of-orthogonality proof mainly invokes delegated polar-factor and nearest-orthogonal results.
The aggregated, mixed-precision, two-sided, Gram-Schmidt, and Givens discussions are chiefly prose expectations or adaptations rather than fully proved finite target results.
The weighted Procrustes conclusion is proved almost entirely by invoking an external orthogonal Procrustes theorem, so it is excluded by the source-selection policy.
Experimental observations and plots are not formal benchmark targets.

T1.decision: Skipped after a fresh full-paper audit. Lemmas 2.1-2.2 require a probabilistic inner-product result that is not in frozen NumStability; Lemmas 4.1-4.3 and Theorem 4.4 require matrix concentration and conditional-expectation machinery that is also absent. Frozen NumStability has substantial deterministic Householder construction, application, and QR results, but those results do not discharge the paper-specific mean-independent probabilistic bounds. Theorem 4.5 and Theorem 6.1 instead depend mainly on delegated polar-factor or Procrustes theorems. Therefore no source-faithful target has exactly one substantial NumStability dependency that would materially speed L over N.

T2.decision: Skipped after the strict source audit. The former equation (3.4) target used two substantial library directions, but the paper explicitly treats the identity as well known and delegates it to Tropp. No other result both belongs to this paper and needs at least two substantial NumStability results.

T3.decision: Use both forms of equations (4.8)-(4.9), retaining the Model 1.5 computed Householder product, the probability-one local bound, a matrix-valued O(u^2) remainder, and the exact Q^T/F_j factor ordering.

selection_policy: Use a finite claim made and proved in this paper.
Reject experiments and claims whose proof is mainly delegated elsewhere; when a selected displayed result contains asymptotic notation, represent that notation explicitly rather than deleting it.
Prefer exact displayed bounds and identities.
Keep the fixed Lean setting condition-neutral and paper-scoped.
Assign tiers only after verified frozen-library searches.
